tasks.description:
**Which of two looks held the stripes?** Each trial shows the observer two looks in turn, each [[param:interval_duration]] long and [[param:isi]] apart, marked by four corner marks around a square field of [[param:field_dva]] on a uniform grey. In one look, chosen at random, the field holds a stationary vertical sine-wave grating at the same mean luminance as the grey; in the other it holds nothing. The observer presses F for the first look or J for the second; the fixation point then turns green or red for [[param:feedback_duration]].

**What changes.** The spatial frequency (cycles per degree, one cell each, interleaved) and, trial by trial, the grating's contrast (Lmax - Lmin) / (Lmax + Lmin), which QUEST+ chooses on a log scale to home in on each cell's threshold.

**What is measured.** Proportion correct as a function of contrast in each cell; the threshold is the contrast for 81% correct in a fitted Weibull function, and the contrast sensitivity is 1 / threshold. Plotted against spatial frequency, sensitivities form the contrast-sensitivity function. The record keeps the contrast asked for and the contrast of the image actually drawn.

**What it can and cannot show.** A drop in sensitivity at low and high frequencies, with a peak between, for this observer on this display. Its absolute values depend on the display's luminance, gamma and bit depth, the field size and the observer's optics; it is not a clinical test. The paper measured thresholds by adjustment ([[task:csf-adjustment]]); forced choice is a deliberate change.
notes: Paper (p. 553): mean 500 cd/m2, contrast switched on and off at 0.5 c/s, 10 x 10 or 2 x 2 cm apertures at 57 or 285 cm (10 or 2 deg), monocular, cycloplegic, 2.5-mm artificial pupil, threshold by adjustment, 5 or 10 settings.
Changed here: two-interval forced choice with QUEST+, binocular natural viewing, a display's luminance instead of 500 cd/m2.
ASSUMED: frequencies, vertical stripes, random phase, 1000-ms looks, 500-ms gap, corner marks, fixation point, feedback, QUEST+ grids, 60 trials per cell.
Contrast below one display code step (about 0.8% on 8 bits) exists only through dithering; set display_bits and measure gamma before real data.

tasks.description:
**The paper's method.** The grating switches on and off once every [[param:flicker_period]] (the paper's 0.5 c/s) inside a square field of [[param:field_dva]], with no change in mean luminance. The observer turns its contrast down or up (arrow keys or scroll wheel, a factor of 10^[[param:knob_step_log10]] per step) until the stripes are barely detectable, then presses SPACE. Each spatial frequency gets [[param:paradigm.n_per_condition]] settings, in random order, each starting from a random contrast.

**What is measured.** The settings; a frequency's threshold is their geometric mean and the sensitivity its reciprocal. Settings depend on the observer's criterion for "barely detectable", which forced choice ([[task:csf-2ifc]]) avoids.
notes: Paper (p. 553): on-off at 0.5 c/s, settings until barely detectable, 5 or 10 per threshold, standard error under 10%.
ASSUMED: equal on and off halves, the knob step, start contrasts, no fixation mark, 5 settings per frequency.
